Mutations in PQBP1 disrupt RNA processing, leading to intellectual disability in Renpenning syndrome. Similarly, mutations in HNRNPA1 disrupt protein handling and can lead to protein aggregation, causing distal muscular dystrophy in Finnish upper limb-onset distal myopathy. Mutations in HNRNPA1 disrupt normal RNA processing, leading to protein aggregation, which underlies the myopathy and neurodegeneration seen in inclusion body myopathy. Similarly, mutations in PQBP1 disrupt RNA processing, contributing to intellectual disability in Renpenning syndrome. Both pathways converge on dysregulated RNA processing and subsequent protein aggregation, impacting neuronal and muscle function.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in HNRNPA1 with a population frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD would significantly weaken the hypothesis of its causal role in inclusion body myopathy with early-onset Paget disease. _(variant: rs1130214)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link through aberrant RNA processing and protein aggregation in Renpenning syndrome and inclusion body myopathy could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative and neuromuscular disorders. Modulating RNA processing or targeting protein aggregation pathways might offer a unified treatment strategy.
